gates.name: detect_garble
gates.decides: Whether a blob of text is 'garbled' (script-aware gibberish/OCR-noise detection); core primitive underlying every garble-related gate.
gates.inputs: text, script_context (ScriptContext: dominant_script, had_presentation_forms, source), config (_garble_config: garble_latin_ratio, garble_nonsense_ratio, garble_digit_floor, etc.), blob_kind (BlobKind.TREE_TEXT etc.)

gates.name: _gate_node_garbling
gates.decides: Gate 4 in GATE_TABLE: fires when per-node garble ratio (garbled-node-count / node_count) exceeds garble_node_ratio_threshold.
gates.inputs: TreeSignals.node_count, _garble_check_nodes(structure, script_context, config) which internally calls detect_garble per node

gates.name: validate_tree
gates.decides: Runs all 10 gates in GATE_TABLE exhaustively; picks primary defect = first firing gate in table order, EXCEPT D4 override: if a non-garble defect fires first but GARBLING/NODE_GARBLING also fired, garble-type defects win as primary so OCR recovery dispatches correctly. Returns TreeGateResult(ok, defect, all_defects, warnings).
gates.inputs: structure, expected_script/ScriptContext, page_count, rtl_decision; builds TreeSignals via TreeSignals.from_tree; thresholds from VerdictThresholds.from_config(pipeline_config)

gates.name: finalize_gate_and_route
gates.decides: Single writer of state.gate_result/ok/reason/first_defect/route, atomically derived from a validate_tree result (or legacy tuple). Calls decide_route(first_defect, flat_routing_enabled) to pick the extraction route.

gates.name: apply_promotions
gates.decides: Zone-4 D1: unconditional structural hard-fail (max_leaf_ratio > hard_fail_max_leaf_ratio) evaluated BEFORE any promotion, with image-enrichment as the only guarded exception. D2: ordered if/elif pipeline (image_enrichment > structural_pass > cat_a(OCR) > cat_b(flat) > cat_c(content_class) > small_doc) — first match wins, but ALL paths are evaluated for telemetry (promotion_paths_matched). A content-volume floor (min_marginal_chars) gates ALL promotion/MARGINAL paths regardless of structural metrics (HR#5). No match -> MARGINAL with a diagnostic reason.
gates.inputs: GateOutcome (defect, signals, all_defects), content_class, image_enrichment_ratio, inspector_class, VerdictThresholds, expected_script, source_selection flag, script_context

gates.name: _try_image_enrichment
gates.decides: Image-enrichment rescue eligibility: content_class in (flat_prose, flat_mixed), image_enrichment_ratio>=0.8, node_count>=3, not effectively_garbled, promoted-text length >= min_image_promoted_chars, and a SECOND detect_garble() call on the deduped/promoted text must also pass clean. VG-7 fix: computed once and shared by both the D1 exception and D2 pipeline in apply_promotions (previously computed twice from two call sites, which could drift).
gates.inputs: TreeSignals, content_class, image_enrichment_ratio, VerdictThresholds, expected_script, script_context

gates.name: _eligible_image_dominant
gates.decides: Image-dominant OCR recovery eligibility for DEPTH_LOW defect: requires state.ok==False, pipeline_config.image_dominant_ocr_escalation_enabled config flag, and TreeDefect.DEPTH_LOW present in ALL active defects (Zone-1 fix: checks all_defects not just first_defect, so DEPTH_LOW firing as a secondary defect still triggers recovery).

gates.name: save_doc_meta
gates.decides: Zone-5: SOLE authoritative entry point for verdict persistence. Read-merge-write onto the .meta.json sidecar (MinIO). Merges verdict/provenance/facet fields onto the existing sidecar so subset-payload callers don't drop fields. Consistency is 'eventual' (no write-visibility barrier) — contrast with save_doc/save_flat_doc which retain a read-after-write barrier. Postgres registry (_upsert_registry_row) is the actual max-priority-wins arbiter (RFC-037 D5); this sidecar just mirrors the arbitrated row.
gates.inputs: doc_id, meta dict (verdict, verdict_reason, max_leaf_ratio, pipeline_version, content_class, node_count, effective_config, etc.)

gates.name: write_verdict
gates.decides: DEPRECATED thin wrapper retained only for legacy callers (promotion_sweep.run_sweep, preprocess_client.recompute_verdicts) — delegates entirely to save_doc_meta. No longer does the old atomic dual-write to both the processed artifact and sidecar.
gates.inputs: doc_id, verdict, verdict_reason, pipeline_version, verdict_computed_at, max_leaf_ratio, content_class

gates.name: read_registry_fields
gates.decides: Projects registry-relevant fields from a persisted processed doc. Verdict-field source priority: (1) artifact body (.json/.flat.json) if present and non-empty [legacy pre-Zone-5 docs only], (2) sidecar (.meta.json) fallback for any verdict field still missing — for Zone-5+ docs the artifact body never carries verdict fields so this ALWAYS falls through to the sidecar.
gates.inputs: doc_id, content_class (selects .flat.json vs .json key); reads MinIO object + _read_existing_sidecar

gates.name: _upsert_registry_row
gates.decides: Worker-parent-process dual-write into Postgres registry via upsert_doc (the actual max-priority-wins verdict arbiter per RFC-037 D5), then mirrors success/failure metrics to Redis. Must run in the long-lived worker parent because the isolated converters_cli child subprocess (where save_doc_meta executes) never opens a registry pool.
gates.inputs: registry fields dict (from read_registry_fields or passed directly), doc_id; calls registry.queries.upsert_doc, registry.schema.get_pool, and on failure _enqueue_verdict_retry

gates.name: _text_layer_has_content
gates.decides: Text-layer probe gating whether picture-level OCR is even attempted — if the PDF's native text layer already has non-garbled content for a region, picture OCR is skipped (calls detect_garble internally on the extracted text layer content).

interactions.detail: Unconditional structural hard-fail (max_leaf_ratio > hard_fail_max_leaf_ratio) is evaluated before D2's ordered promotion pipeline; only the image_enrichment path is allowed as a guarded exception to the hard-fail, all other D2 promotion paths (structural_pass, cat_a, cat_b, cat_c, small_doc) are unreachable once hard-fail fires.

Content-volume floor (stripped flat_text length < th.min_marginal_chars) short-circuits straight to FAIL before any promotion/MARGINAL path is tried, regardless of otherwise-passing structural metrics — closes a documented HR#5 hysteresis gap (Zone-8).

When GARBLING/NODE_GARBLING co-fires with a non-garble defect, validate_tree forces the garble defect to be primary_defect even if a different gate fired first in GATE_TABLE order, specifically so downstream OCR-recovery routing dispatches correctly on the garble path rather than the other co-firing defect.

detect_garble is invoked independently on two different text derivations of the same document — sig.flat_text during validate_tree's gate table, and a separately deduped/promoted text blob (_dedupe_chart_text_lines(sig.primary_text)) inside _try_image_enrichment — a second, textually-divergent garble check that could in principle disagree with the first.

Zone-3 fix: finalize_gate_and_route is now the SOLE writer of gate_result/ok/reason/first_defect/route; it replaced three call sites that previously each set a subset of these five fields independently, which had created a stale-routing race window.

Zone-5 downgraded write_verdict to a thin pass-through wrapper around save_doc_meta; it no longer performs its former atomic dual-write to both the processed artifact and the sidecar. Only legacy callers (promotion_sweep.run_sweep, preprocess_client.recompute_verdicts) still invoke write_verdict at all — trace_path found zero live in-repo callers besides tests/legacy scripts.

Two possible sources for the same verdict fields: the processed-doc JSON body (checked first, legacy pre-Zone-5 docs only) and the .meta.json sidecar (fallback, and in practice the ONLY populated source for all Zone-5+ docs since new artifacts never embed verdict fields in the body).

Sequential cross-process cascade: save_doc_meta runs inside the isolated converters_cli child subprocess (no registry pool available there by design) and writes the MinIO sidecar; the long-lived worker parent then calls _upsert_registry_row -> upsert_doc after the child returns to perform the actual Postgres dual-write, which registry.queries.upsert_doc treats as the final max-priority-wins arbiter per RFC-037 D5. If this ordering is violated, verdicts could persist to MinIO without ever reaching Postgres.

DEPTH_LOW defect has only one recovery path (image-dominant OCR); the config flag check happens inside the eligibility gate itself so the whole recovery mechanism is skipped entirely when disabled, rather than being gated at the call site.

Zone-8 fix: the source_selection flag bypasses _clamp_pass (which enforces bidi-degraded/depth-inadequacy caps) ONLY for the image_enrichment promotion path; every other promotion path always flows through _clamp_pass regardless of source_selection, closing a prior scope leak.

If the native PDF text layer already has non-garbled content for a region, picture-level Tesseract/VLM OCR is skipped entirely for that region — the garble probe on extracted text is upstream of and suppresses the OCR-escalation subsystem.

flags.name: pipeline_config.image_dominant_ocr_escalation_enabled
flags.controls: Whether _eligible_image_dominant allows DEPTH_LOW-triggered image-dominant OCR recovery to fire at all.

flags.name: pipeline_config.allow_agpl_fallback / agpl_structural_fallback_enabled
flags.controls: Whether the AGPL-licensed pymupdf4llm converter is included in the converter fallback chain (CLAUDE.md Hard Rule 4); structural-failure fall-through to AGPL converter is gated separately from generic transient-failure fallback.

flags.name: pipeline_config.verdict_downgrade_enabled
flags.controls: Whether verdict downgrade logic is active in the indexer wiring (per test_verdict.TestVerdictDowngradeEnabled).

flags.name: pipeline_config.ocr_escalation_garble / ocr_escalation_per_picture / ocr_escalation_low_content
flags.controls: Three independent triggers for escalating to OCR: garble-detected text, per-picture region OCR, and low-content-density documents.

flags.name: flat_routing_enabled
flags.controls: Whether a failing tree gate can route to the flat-extraction fallback path instead of a terminal reject; test_gates.TestFinalizeAtomicity.test_flat_routing_disabled_reject confirms disabling it forces REJECT.

flags.name: converter_transient_retry_count
flags.controls: Retry budget for transient converter subprocess failures before falling through the converter chain (e.g. to AGPL fallback).

flags.name: remote_version_enforce
flags.controls: Whether a remote-converter version skew (RemoteVersionSkewError) is treated as fatal.

flags.name: apply_promotions(source_selection=...)
flags.controls: Scoped bypass of the bidi/depth _clamp_pass caps, restricted to the image_enrichment promotion path only (Zone-8 fix narrowed this from a broader bypass).

flags.name: OPENAI_BASE_URL
flags.controls: Routing lever for PII-bearing documents to a no-training/zero-retention LLM tier (CLAUDE.md Hard Rule 3).

observations: Verdict persistence is a two-tier cascade with an explicit process boundary: save_doc_meta (MinIO sidecar, eventual consistency, runs in the isolated converters_cli child subprocess) happens first, then the worker parent process performs the actual authoritative Postgres write via _upsert_registry_row -> upsert_doc (RFC-037 D5's 'max-priority-wins arbiter'). This means the sidecar can transiently disagree with Postgres, and any code path that reads verdict from the sidecar without accounting for this window risks staleness — read_registry_fields explicitly documents this as the reason it falls back to the sidecar only when the artifact body is empty.

detect_garble is the single core primitive but is invoked from at least 7 distinct call sites across 3 subsystems (validate_tree's gate table via _gate_node_garbling/_garble_check_flat_blocks, _try_image_enrichment's promotion rescue, _text_layer_has_content's OCR-skip probe, _document_level_text_fallback, _attempt_tesseract_raster_recovery, _recover_picture_text) — each passing a different derived text blob and ScriptContext, which is the documented source of the VG-6/VG-7/Zone-8 'divergence' bugs the codebase has been actively fixing (per apply_promotions docstring history).

apply_promotions' docstring itself documents its own audit history in unusual detail (RFC-040 D1/D2, Zone-8 fixes, VG-6/VG-7 verdict-gate-cascade fixes) — this function has clearly been the repeated site of promotion-path divergence bugs and is treated as the canonical single source of truth for the verdict decision, consistent with CLAUDE.md Hard Rule 5 (never silently persist a low-quality tree).

finalize_gate_and_route is a deliberately-introduced 'single writer' pattern (Zone-3) collapsing what were three independent field-setting call sites into one atomic derivation — a textbook fix for a 'competing writers to the same fields' architectural smell, and a useful template for the analogous save_doc_meta/write_verdict consolidation (Zone-5) and the _try_image_enrichment dedup (VG-7).

write_verdict has zero live production callers per trace_path (only legacy promotion_sweep.run_sweep and preprocess_client.recompute_verdicts, both explicitly called out in its own docstring as deprecated-but-retained) — a candidate for eventual removal once those two scripts are migrated to call save_doc_meta directly.

The garble-gate ordering fix in validate_tree (D4: garble-type defects always win as primary when co-firing with any other gate) is a clear 'suppresses/overrides' architectural pattern: it exists specifically so downstream recovery dispatch (which branches on primary defect) reliably lands on garble-specific OCR recovery rather than a structural-only recovery path that wouldn't fix garbled text.

PipelineConfig (src/pageindex_mcp/config.py:364-577) centralizes ~45 tunable fields covering garble thresholds, OCR escalation triggers, promotion-path char floors, and AGPL/converter toggles — nearly every gate discussed above pulls its threshold or enable-flag from this single frozen(-per-job) config object via VerdictThresholds.from_config(pipeline_config), so a single reset_pipeline_config() call is the blast radius for changing verdict behavior fleet-wide.

OCR escalation has three independently-gated trigger conditions (garble, per-picture, low-content) plus a fourth structural-failure/image-dominant path (_eligible_image_dominant, DEPTH_LOW-specific) — these are separate gates rather than a unified 'should we OCR' decision, meaning a document could plausibly satisfy one trigger and not another, and the recovery mixin (client/recovery.py) has distinct handler methods per trigger (_recover_image_dominant_ocr, _recover_vlm_fallback, _execute_ocr_retry).
